body_html:
How to think about it

Some things are natural, such as stones, trees and sand; others are made by people, such as chairs, pencils and bottles. Human-made things are made from materials such as wood, metal, glass, clay, cloth and plastic.

Materials have different properties: a stone is hard and cotton is soft; sandpaper is rough and glass is smooth; wood floats and iron sinks. We choose glass for windows because we can see through it and plastic for raincoats because water cannot pass through.

Example

Is a brick natural or human-made?

made from clay by people

Answer: human-made

Example

Which feels rough: sandpaper or a mirror?

touch it

Answer: sandpaper

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all things made of wood are natural.
  • Thinking every heavy thing sinks.
  • Thinking plastic rots quickly.

faq.q: What is the difference between natural and human-made things?
faq.a: Natural things come from nature; human-made things are made by people, often from natural materials.

faq.q: Why are windows made of glass?
faq.a: Light can pass through glass, so we can see out and the room stays bright.
